verdict.rationale: Proton Pass client source is publicly inspectable. There is a public GitHub repo for the Android app with build instructions, a Proton reply linking to github.com/protonpass, and community reports that the iOS and Android clients are open source. One user cites the browser extension's source code, which shows real community review. Coverage is partial because no first-party Proton docs in the pack state the open-source policy, and evidence for the desktop and CLI clients is absent. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the open-source licensing and scope, evidence that the desktop (Windows/macOS/Linux) and CLI clients are open source, and evidence of independent audits or formal community review of the code that handles seeds and secrets.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: If you want to build the app locally, please refer to the [BUILD.md](./docs/public/BUILD.md) file.
And it is open source: https://github.com/protonpass
User notes only the iOS and Android clients are open source, not the server implementation
From the extension's source code, telemetry is anonymous but always sent to a remote endpoint.
